residencyRequirements.description: The plaintiff must be domiciled in Alaska at the time of filing. There is no minimum duration of residency required.

waitingPeriod.description: Alaska requires a 30-day waiting period after service of process before the court may enter a decree. (AS 25.24.090)

noFault.name: Incompatibility of Temperament
noFault.description: The parties have an incompatibility of temperament that has caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage

fault.name: Willful Desertion
fault.description: Willful desertion for a period of one year

fault.name: Cruel Treatment
fault.description: Either cruel and inhuman treatment calculated to impair health or endanger life

fault.name: Habitual Gross Drunkenness
fault.description: Habitual gross drunkenness contracted since marriage and continuing for one year prior to filing

fault.name: Incurable Mental Illness
fault.description: Incurable mental illness when the spouse has been confined to an institution for at least 18 months

fault.name: Personal Indignities
fault.description: Personal indignities by one spouse making life burdensome for the other

fault.name: Failure to Consummate
fault.description: Failure to consummate the marriage at the time of marriage

groundsForDissolution.notes: Alaska allows both fault and no-fault grounds. Incompatibility of temperament is the most common (no-fault) ground.

propertyDivision.description: Alaska follows equitable distribution. The court divides marital property in a fair and just manner, considering factors such as length of marriage, earning capacity, financial condition, conduct, and desirability of awarding the family home to the custodial parent.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before marriage or by inheritance/gift is generally considered separate property, though the court may consider it in achieving a fair division.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirements — domicile in Alaska; 30-day waiting period after service
Grounds for divorce — fault and no-fault
Alaska Child Support Guidelines — percentage of income model

filingFees.notes: Alaska filing fees are approximately $250 for a divorce complaint but may vary by judicial district. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Financial Declaration (DR-250)
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on defendant via process server or certified mail

service.name: Waiver of Service
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Custody and Visitation Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing custody and visitation

withChildren.name: Child Support Order (DR-305)
withChildren.description: Calculation per Alaska Child Support Guidelines (Civil Rule 90.3)

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Affidavit (DR-306)
withChildren.description: Income and deduction information for child support calculation

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Alaska Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Alaska must file an answer within 20 days of service (additional time may be granted)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Alaska uses a percentage of income model under Civil Rule 90.3. Child support is calculated as a percentage of the non-custodial parent's adjusted annual income based on the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be manifestly unjust.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Alaska courts may award alimony in a divorce action. The court considers the length of the marriage, the station in life and circumstances of the parties, the age and health of the parties, the earning capacity of each party, the financial condition of each party, and the conduct of the parties.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Either party may request alimony. There is no fixed formula — the court has discretion to award temporary, rehabilitative, or permanent alimony based on the circumstances.

court.name: Superior Court
court.description: Divorce is filed in the Superior Court in the judicial district where either party resides. (AS 22.10)
